analysis.evidence: In בְּנֵי יֶפֶת, the construct noun בְּנֵי means ‘sons of’ and יֶפֶת names their father. The list of his sons begins with גֹּמֶר.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: גֹּמֶר is the first name after בְּנֵי יֶפֶת (‘sons of Japheth’). The following וּמָגוֹג (‘and Magog’) continues the list, confirming that גֹּמֶר is a personal name here.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Add a Hebrew personal-name article for מָגוֹג. The genealogy supports the gloss “Magog” and gives no basis for “dainties” or the proposed root גוב.
draft.definition: Magog is the personal name of one of Japheth’s sons.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:2 identifies Magog by his place in the genealogy. The verse gives no etymology for his name.

analysis.evidence: בְּנֵי יֶפֶת means “the sons of Japheth” and introduces the list in Genesis 10:2. Magog is the second name in that list, between Gomer and Madai.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וּ means “and” and joins the personal name מָגוֹג to the preceding name גֹּמֶר.
